issues.legal_issue: Whether an arbitration award affecting immovable property was presented for registration within time when it remained in court custody during judicial proceedings and was presented immediately after being returned.
material_facts: The arbitrators made an award affecting immovable property and filed it in court before the ordinary registration period expired.
The award remained in court custody from its filing until it was returned to the arbitrators; the court declined their application to obtain it earlier.
An injunction also prevented the arbitrators from taking steps while it was in force.
The arbitrators presented the award for registration the day after they regained possession of it.
The registering officer treated the presentation as timely by excluding the period during which the judicial proceedings were pending.
issues.conclusion: The award was presented for registration within time. The period during which it remained in court custody was to be excluded, and the High Court's order quashing registration was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 23 and 25 of the Registration Act, 1908, read together, allow a total of up to eight months for presentation when the conditions in section 25 are met. Applying the principle in section 15 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the period during which the award was held in court and could not be presented was excluded. The maxims actus curiae neminem gravabit and lex non cogit ad impossibilia support that result: a court's act should not prejudice a person, and the law does not require the impossible. Nityananda M. Joshi v. Life Insurance Corporation of India was distinguished; M. Venkataratnam v. M. Chelamayya was referred to. The Court accepted that an award affecting immovable property must be registered.

rule.if: award_registration_limitation_dispute and award_affects_immovable_property and award_filed_in_court_before_registration_period_expired and award_remained_in_court_custody and parties_could_not_present_award_while_in_custody and award_presented_immediately_after_return

predicates.award_registration_limitation_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether an arbitration award was presented for registration within the applicable time.
predicates.award_affects_immovable_property: The arbitrators made an award concerning rights in immovable property.
predicates.award_filed_in_court_before_registration: The award was filed in court before the ordinary period for presenting it for registration expired.
predicates.award_remained_in_court_custody: The award stayed in court custody until the court returned it to the arbitrators.
predicates.parties_could_not_present_award_while_in: The arbitrators or parties could not present the award for registration while it was held by the court.
predicates.award_presented_immediately_after_return: The arbitrators presented the award for registration immediately after the court returned it.

issues.definition: When an award affecting immovable property is the subject of a registration-timeliness dispute, was filed in court before the ordinary period expired, could not be presented while held there, and was presented immediately after its return, its presentation is treated as timely.
